stories.title: At least 109 dead including children after migrant boat capsizes off Djibouti

Photograph: Luis Tato/AFP/Getty Images At least 109 dead including children after migrant boat capsizes off Djibouti More than 116 others still missing from vessel that was heading to Yemen with 350 people onboard, UN agency says At least 109 people, including 15 children, have died after a boat carrying 350 migrants capsized off the coast of Djibouti, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has said. More than 116 others remain missing after the incident, which, according to survivors, happened near Guhere, north of the fishing town of Obock, during the night of 8-9 October when the boat was travelling from Djibouti to Yemen. Fifty-two of the bodies recovered were men, while 42 were women and 15 children, the UN agency said.

stories.summary: Sahel: le nombre de déplacés au Burkina Faso, au Mali et au Niger a presque doublé depuis 2020, selon le HCR Le Haut Commissariat des Nations unies pour les réfugiés (HCR) alerte sur la crise des déplacements au Sahel : le Mali, le Burkina Faso et le Niger comptent désormais près de 4 millions de déplacés et de réfugiés, presque deux fois plus qu'en 2020, année du premier coup d'État militaire à Bamako. Publié le : 11/10/2026 - 05:02 2 min Temps de lecture Un camp de déplacés au Burkina Faso, en mai 2024. © FANNY NOARO-KABRE / AFP Par : David Baché | AFP Publicité Lire la suite Au Mali, au Burkina Faso et au Niger, « les incidents sécuritaires ont presque doublé depuis 2020, affaiblissant la présence de l'État [...] et augmentant les risques tant pour les personnes déplacées que pour les communautés d'accueil », a déclaré Abdouraouf Gnon-Konde, directeur du HCR pour l'Afrique de l'Ouest et l'Afrique centrale, vendredi 9 octobre. Les militaires qui ont pris le pouvoir au Mali en 2020, au Burkina Faso en 2022 et au Niger en 2023, et qui ont créé ensemble l' Alliance des États du Sahel (AES) pour lutter contre les groupes jihadistes ou indépendantistes actifs sur leur territoire, disent pourtant faire de la sécurité des populations leur priorité. Ils vantent aussi régulièrement la « montée en puissance » de leurs armées et les victoires accumulées, selon eux, face aux « terroristes » - justifiant ainsi au passage leur maintien au pouvoir sans élections. Mais les violences des groupes armés « terroristes » et celles des armées nationales et de leurs supplétifs ont continué d'augmenter, obligeant de plus en plus les populations civiles à fuir.

The fighting in Heiban and Kauda and surrounding areas in the Nuba Mountains has killed more than 500 people from the Atoro ethnic group, displaced over 25,000, and burnt dozens of villages, according to local tribal leaders. While Ayin was unable to verify these estimates, the conflict data research organisation ACLED recorded 49 incidents of infighting, resulting in at least 158 deaths between March and August this year. Local sources told Ayin that the warring factions have agreed to a cessation of hostilities to allow the mediation initiative to proceed. But a seat at the table is far from guaranteed: Ghana will have to convince all 11 existing members it is a valuable new partner. Joining Brics would open up Ghana's economic options, Foreign Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa said when he announced plans to formally apply for membership on Wednesday. "It] will diversify our base and our partnerships and will also allow us to have more cooperation within the Global South framework," he said. Seeking deeper engagement with other emerging powers, Accra says joining Brics would complement, rather than replace, its existing relationships with the International Monetary Fund, World Bank and other traditional partners. stories.summary: Africa: In Conversation with Mariama Camara, a Guinean textile entrepreneur building global institutions behind unique African textiles Bird Story Agency Guinean textile entrepreneur Mariama Camara 10 October 2026 Bird Story Agency (Africa) interview By Bonface Orucho Guinean textile entrepreneur Mariama Camara is moving from promoting African textiles globally to building the institutions behind the industry. Through the Institute of African Textiles, she is pushing for greater ownership, protection and commercial value for the knowledge held by African makers. African textile designer Mariama Camara believes the next phase of Africa's textile industry must move beyond global recognition towards ownership, stronger institutions and greater economic value for the people who hold its knowledge. Camara has spent more than two decades working with artisans across Africa and taking their textiles into global fashion. Her collaborations have included Tory Burch, Ulla Johnson, LemLem and EDUN, helping bring "Made in Africa" textiles into major international markets while keeping the women and artisans who make them at the centre of the story.

stories.title: Questions remain over Ebola patient who travelled across three nations undetected
stories.summary: Image source, EPA Image caption, Nearly 70 potential contacts have been placed under quarantine in Nairobi By Wycliffe Muia Published 10 October 2026 A Kenyan businessman was able to spend time in one of the regions worst-affected by Ebola, then travel to two more countries before his illness was identified. The 40-year-old - who was only diagnosed with the deadly infectious disease after arriving seriously ill at a Nairobi hospital - became Kenya's first confirmed case. He died two days later on 5 October. That his infection went undetected at multiple health facilities in the Democratic Republic of Congo and two airport health screenings in Uganda and Kenya has raised serious questions about these nations' biosecurity during a significant outbreak. More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak to date.

The Nigerian star will become the first African artist to headline one of the American football league's international games when the Philadelphia Eagles take on the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday. Ahead of the performance at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Starr told BBC Newsbeat her history-making performance "itself is a message". stories.summary: Fraught with danger … Jasmine Jobson in In the Shadows View image in fullscreen Fraught with danger … Jasmine Jobson in In the Shadows Review In the Shadows review – true tale of Ramla Ali’s remarkable rise through the boxing ranks is a knockout Jasmine Jobson goes the distance as the British-Somalian boxer battling pain from her past and her family’s disapproval in a heavyweight, tick-the-boxes production T he true-life success story of boxer Ramla Ali is confidently told in this capable picture from screenwriter Ursula Rani Sarma and documentary director Anthony Wonke, in his feature-film debut. Ali is the British-Somali boxer who escaped to the UK from the Somali civil war with her family as a refugee, and in 2021 became the first person to box for Somalia at Olympic Games . The boxing significance of her last name is actually not mentioned in the film – and I never noticed it until it flashed up in a kind of “fight card” intertitle before her first competitive bout. She is fiercely played by Jasmine Jobson, from TV’s Top Boy; her supportive white Muslim-convert husband Richard – a hugely important figure in enabling Ramla to break away from her disapproving family and do as she wants – is played by Finn Cole, and her abusive trainer Clinton is Gershwyn Eustache Jr. This is a film that takes you through the classic boxing-movie scenes fluently enough: the nervous first appearance in the gym, the overbearing quasi-parental coach, the heartstopping fight debut.

Geneva, 7 October 2026 – Vaccine programmes supported by Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance (Gavi) generated more than US$ 30 billion in economic benefits in 2025, the highest annual total in the Alliance's history, according to Gavi's annual report published today . These gains came from preventing illness, death and long-term disability, sparing countries healthcare and wider societal costs, and ultimately helping children achieve higher educational attainment, leading to a longer, more productive working life. In the same year, lower-income countries contributed a record US$ 301 million towards the cost of Gavi-supported vaccines through Gavi's co-financing model, under which countries progressively assume a greater share of vaccine costs as their economies grow. This reflects a broader trajectory: over the last five years, countries have matched the total they contributed over the previous 13 years combined, and from 2026–2030 implementing countries are projected to fund nearly 50% of the costs of their vaccines. He called himself "Sir Wicknell", a nod to the embellishment that epitomised his lifestyle - and a nickname some used for the 45-year-old who packed enough controversy into his short life to last several lifetimes. He was relentlessly self-documenting, building much of his public persona on social media, where he posed with piles of cash and announced the cars and money he gave to people whom he considered deserving. Chivayo delighted in displaying his access to heads of state across Africa and showing off his possessions, conducting video tours of his fleet of expensive cars, mainly Rolls-Royces, with vanity plates, watches and a vast collection of designer shoes.
